rounds.proof_sketch: Kernel launches with 1D block: threads_per_block=256. In 1D launches, blockDim.x=256, blockDim.y=1. Original: shared_sum = shared_mem + 256 (non-overlapping). Mutant: shared_sum = shared_mem + 1 (overlapping). However, the algorithm is sequential: (1) max reduction uses shared_max[0..255] and stores result in shared_mem[0], (2) after sync, row_max is read from shared_mem[0], (3) sum values written to shared_sum[tid] = shared_mem[1+tid], i.e., indices 1-256. Critically, shared_mem[0] is NEVER overwritten by shared_sum writes since shared_sum starts at index 1. The sum reduction then operates correctly on shared_mem[1..256].
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the shared_sum pointer offset from blockDim.x (256) to blockDim.y (1) in a 1D kernel launch. While this creates overlapping memory regions between shared_max and shared_sum, the algorithm's sequential execution pattern prevents any data hazard. The max reduction completes entirely before any writes to shared_sum occur. The critical value (row_max) is stored at shared_mem[0], which is never touched by the mutant's shared_sum writes since shared_sum[0] maps to shared_mem[1]. Since blockDim.y is always 1 for 1D kernel launches (as configured by the host code with threads_per_block=256), this mutation produces bitwise-identical results to the original.
rounds.kill_strategy: UNKILLABLE - The mutant is semantically equivalent under the fixed kernel configuration. The only way to kill this mutant would be to change the kernel launch to use 2D block dimensions (e.g., dim3 block(16, 16)), which would require configuration changes not permitted under the testing contract. No value-level test can distinguish the mutant from the original.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for CUDA kernels should flag mutations involving dimension indices (x/y/z) as potentially equivalent when kernels use lower-dimensional launches. Future test frameworks could inject alternate launch configurations (1D vs 2D vs 3D blocks) as part of the mutation-killing strategy, or the mutation tool could detect 1D launches and skip mutations that substitute blockDim.y/z for blockDim.x.
